messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@snlabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T22:22:00Z
Subject: Synapse Labs — Reserved Fleet: traffic & capacity snapshot

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we evaluate a reserved (dedicated) fleet with Redwood, the pre-sales team asked that we share a concise traffic snapshot so you can recommend an appropriate GPU mix and commit level. High level answers below — I'm attaching a small CSV with representative 7-day telemetry.

Quick answers:
- Primary workload: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + embedding-based similarity searches for real-time support.
- Typical prompt size: 40--120 tokens; average response: 220 tokens (95th percentile 600).
- Avg requests/sec (sustained): 3.6 rps; peak 95th-minute: 28 rps; short-lived spikes up to ~45 rps.
- Session model: short-lived sessions (stateless), many single-turn RAG calls. KV cache reuse limited.
- Target P95 latency: 250–350ms end-to-end for generation.

Attachments: synapse_traffic_week.csv (CSV, 18 KB) — includes per-minute request counts and token histograms.

Are there specific additional fields you need for a sizing estimate (burst duration distribution, concurrency vs sustained breakdown, cold-start tolerance)?

Best,
Elena
Director of Engineering
Synapse Labs
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@snlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Synapse Labs — Reserved Fleet: traffic & capacity snapshot

Hi Elena — thanks for the CSV and the summary, this helps a lot. A couple quick clarifying asks before we size a recommended reserved pool: 

1) Burst shape: can you indicate whether the 45 rps spikes are sustained over multiple minutes (e.g., 5–10 min) or are single-minute microbursts? If you can point us to a percentile by minute we can better model queueing vs short-term burst pools.
2) Token mix over the day: does average response length vary by time-of-day (we typically see longer responses during batch/reporting windows).
3) SLO & fallback tolerance: if we route to a lower-precision quantized model variant during extreme tail, is that acceptable for non-critical traffic?
4) Any outbound compliance constraints (no model logs exported outside region) — call that out so we recommend Private vs Dedicated.

I've attached our short pre-sales intake sheet (redwood_pre_sales_template.xlsx) — fill just the green fields and send back. Marissa (SE) and Karthik (capacity lead) are CC'd and will run a quick internal estimate once we have the burst duration and token-by-hour.

Next steps: if you prefer, we can schedule a 45-minute sizing workshop (we'll run a small simulation and present a recommended GPU mix + fallback policy). Book here: https://cal.com/vanessa/redwood-sizing-workshop

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pre_sales_template.xlsx (XLSX, 24 KB)
From: Elena Park <elena@snlabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@snapslabs-infra.com>
Date: 2026-10-27T08:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Synapse Labs — Reserved Fleet: traffic & capacity snapshot

Vanessa — thanks, answers inline below and I attached a cleaned per-minute percentile export.

1) Burst duration: our 95th-minute spikes are typically 3–7 minutes long (mostly end-of-day customer syncs and marketing-driven traffic). The 99th-minute can hit short ~1–2 minute microbursts at unpredictable times.
2) Token mix by hour: daytime support hours show average responses ~180 tokens; nightly batch processes produce longer outputs (~450 tokens) but are lower QPS. Peak-day evenings (US PST) tend to have the longest responses.
3) Fallback tolerance: for token-cost reasons we'd accept a quantized 8-bit variant for up to 10% of traffic during emergency fallback windows, but prefer to reserve highest-precision model for 90%+ of production calls.
4) Compliance: all model logs must remain within our US account and cannot be replicated to EU without explicit approval.

Attachment: synapse_traffic_week_agg.csv (CSV, 66 KB) — per-minute 7-day percentiles plus token-length distribution.

We're happy to run the sizing workshop this week; Alex will coordinate availability. Also please share a rough nightly cost estimate for the proposed reserved footprint (order-of-magnitude) so we can prep procurement.

Thanks,
Elena
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@snlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T14:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Synapse Labs — Reserved Fleet: traffic & capacity snapshot

Elena — perfect, this is exactly what we need. Summary of immediate next steps:

- Marissa/Karthik: we'll ingest synapse_traffic_week_agg.csv into our sizing simulator and return a recommended SKU mix (likely a hybrid pool: NVL8-equivalent for most traffic + small high-memory SKUs for long-response night batches). Expect an initial sizing note and cost ballpark by EOD 2026-11-02.
- Elena/Alex: please confirm a 45-minute workshop slot here: https://cal.com/vanessa/redwood-sizing-workshop — we've reserved a few slots Thursday/Friday PST.
- Procurement ask: if Synapse wants a draft commitment term and order-of-magnitude monthly cost for internal review, I'll pull a quick estimator for a 6/12-month commit once sizing is done.
- Compliance note: we'll flag region-locking in the Private vs Dedicated decision doc; our Solutions team will outline how audit logs and KMS integration work for US-only retention.

I'll also open a HubSpot deal record and attach the sizing artifacts: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/98765

If you can send a signed NDA (DocuSign link) we'll be able to include a fuller telemetry export in the sizing simulation.

Thanks — talk soon.
Vanessa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
